title: Learning Session: Introduction to WebAssembly
summary: A tutorial-style session covering WebAssembly fundamentals, compilation pipeline, and use cases for performance-critical web applications. Focus was on understanding concepts rather than making project decisions.

topics.name: What is WebAssembly
topics.insight: WebAssembly (Wasm) is a binary instruction format that runs in a sandboxed virtual machine inside browsers. It is not a replacement for JavaScript but a complement for CPU-intensive tasks.

topics.name: Compilation Pipeline
topics.insight: Languages like Rust, C, and Go compile to .wasm modules via toolchains like wasm-pack (Rust) or Emscripten (C/C++). The browser loads and instantiates these modules through the WebAssembly JavaScript API.

topics.name: Performance Characteristics
topics.insight: Wasm achieves near-native speed for numerical computation and data processing. For DOM manipulation, JavaScript remains faster because Wasm must cross the JS-Wasm boundary for every DOM call.
